about: The story after the altars (src/Echo.cpp). Act II: once six cities are free each class's hidden quest wakes (sheet: eggs); finishing it makes the Greybeards call and the class's wonder waits on its pedestal in the Reliquary beneath High Hrothgar (wonders: one per class, in class order Summoner, Destruction, Ranger, Spellsword - the ids are the pedestals' old keys). Act III: with all four wonders won (a party pools theirs), three dragons wake at their places (words rows 0-2); each comes at night after a siege of the dead and gives a lasting power. Act IV: with the three dead, the Echo of Alduin waits on the Throat of the World (row 3); its fall breaks the curse and opens the Hall of the Awakened. Positions in Skyrim units (Tamriel or the HighHrothgar cell); yaw in degrees, clockwise from north.

wonders.label: Horn of the Spectral Wyrm
wonders.text: A horn of dragon bone. Blow it and Calling of the Conjurer's Spectral Dragon answers, fighting at your side for a minute - until the three dragons fall, then it stays until it is slain.

wonders.label: Tome of the Six Fires
wonders.text: One cast looses the top spell of all six of your element ladders on the dead round you. Once the three dragons fall, their runes and storms are left burning on the ground too.

wonders.label: Subsuming Vortex
wonders.text: A bow of black-violet steel. Every arrow tears open a black hole where it lands: the dead are dragged in, then it bursts. Once the three dragons fall, the holes grow wider and pull harder.

wonders.label: Dragon Slayer
wonders.text: The Akaviri dragon slayer. Every hit carries the spell in your other hand. Once the three dragons fall, a power attack sends that spell down the line.

Riverwood.echo: We raised this altar in the valley where the river runs out of the mountains, and cut the valley's words into its heart-stone. Vahlok, the cult's jailor, watched us do it from the barrow on the peak. He swore to Alduin that no prisoner of his would ever go free - and the dead, to him, are prisoners.
Riverwood.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Whiterun.echo: The plains' altar is the one Nahkriin hates most, for it stands nearest the road to Sovngarde. He kept that road for Alduin at Skuldafn. When the World-Eater's mist lies on the door, Nahkriin will come to the plains to keep it there.
Whiterun.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Solitude.echo: Volsung could breathe on the peaks where we could not, and he laughed at our altar under the cliffs of Haafingar. But the Voice carries further than breath. The runes on its heart-stone hold the words that answer him.
Solitude.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Windhelm.echo: Zahkriisos was not of this land; he came over the Sea of Ghosts with the cult's fleet, and the cold came with him. We set the altar of the east by the water so that it would hear him first if he ever came back across the ice.
Windhelm.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Markarth.echo: Even the cult feared Otar. They walled him up in Ragnvald while he still breathed. We did not trust the wall, so we raised an altar on the Reach's stone and cut into it words he could not shout down.
Markarth.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Riften.echo: Rahgot's people drank poison sooner than see him taken. A priest who can ask that of his followers will ask it again. When he rises, the Rift's dead will come with him, and the altar must be woken to send them back.
Riften.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Falkreath.echo: Krosis wept for a thousand years at Shearpoint, guarding a word no one came to learn. Grief is a long oath. The altar of the pines is cut with gentler words than the rest - to put children back to sleep.
Falkreath.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Morthal.echo: Hevnoraak's own servants sealed him in Valthume, and set the seal with his blood. No seal holds against SLEN TIID VO. When the marsh fog thickens, look to the altar, and to the words on its heart-stone.
Morthal.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Dawnstar.echo: Vokun's shadows reached into men's dreams. The priests at the temple on the hill dreamed of him for a thousand years before he came. Wake the altar, and the town will sleep without dreaming of him again.
Dawnstar.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

Winterhold.echo: Morokei held the Staff of Magnus in Bromjunaar, and the mages who came after us have never forgotten him. The northern altar stands on the cliffs where the storms break; its words are cut deepest of all, for he is the strongest of them.
Winterhold.by: set down by a Tongue of the Way of the Voice, after Jurgen Windcaller

words.about: Act III and IV (src/Echo.cpp): rows 0-2 are Alduin's three words, each a dragon; row 3 is the Echo of Alduin. Once all four class wonders are won the three dragons wake together, each at its own place and only at night: come near and its siege begins (waves of the dead round the place), and when the last wave falls the dragon comes. Kill it and its word is silenced for good - a power that stays with you. With all three dead the Echo of Alduin waits on the summit of the Throat of the World. Saved in UN_EchoWords (bit per row; bit 8: Act III told). waves/elites per wave, health: x a zombie's night health.

rows.site: the cult's old shrine in the Reach
rows.wake: SLEN. The ground shakes under the Reach. Slenvahrin, the dragon who carried Alduin's first word, circles the cult's old shrine - and the barrow-dead around it grow new flesh to meet you.
rows.silenced: Slenvahrin crashes onto the shrine and burns away to bone. SLEN is silenced: the strength Alduin poured into the dead now runs in you.
rows.power: Flesh Remade: every weapon, bow, spell and wonder hits 15% harder.

rows.wake: TIID. Under Labyrinthian, the great tomb of Bromjunaar, the dragon cult laid its dead by the thousand. Tiidrah, keeper of the second word, gives them back the years the grave took - and every one of them hears it.
rows.silenced: Tiidrah falls across the courtyard of Bromjunaar. TIID is silenced: the time the dead stole is yours now.
rows.power: Borrowed Time: the night's blows hurt you 20% less.

rows.site: the dragon lair on Mount Anthor
rows.wake: VO. On the frozen peak of Mount Anthor, Vonahlok - the Undoing - keeps the last of Alduin's words. Where it flies, death itself comes undone, and the dead of the Pale climb the mountain to its call.
rows.silenced: Vonahlok's shout dies on the wind over Mount Anthor. VO is silenced: the Undoing has undone its last.
rows.power: The Curse Undone: your magicka returns half again as fast.

rows.site: the summit of the Throat of the World
rows.wake: The three words are silent, and only their maker is left. On the summit of the Throat of the World, where the Tongues once cast Alduin out of time, his echo still circles - and the dead of all Skyrim answer it one last time. Climb the mountain at night and end the curse.
rows.silenced: The Echo of Alduin breaks apart over the summit and its voice is gone from the world. The Curse of Alduin is broken: the dead of Skyrim sleep, and the nights are only nights again.
rows.power: The Curse Broken: the Hall of the Awakened opens beneath High Hrothgar.
